Subject: Cross-region MAP: latency & TTFT stress plan + preliminary readout

Tom —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed on the call, the next step in the MAP is a short, focused performance sweep to validate multi-region routing and failover behavior for the flows you plan to ship in Q2. The goal is to verify:

- TTFT (time-to-first-token) for your 3 canonical prompt templates at 64/256/1024 token windows
- Sustained throughput at target concurrency (100/300/800 concurrent sessions)
- Regional latencies from your major egress locations (US east/west, EU, APAC) and cross-region failover time under simulated outage

Proposed cadence:
1) Quick calibration run (US) — 3/29 morning (PST) — 2 hours
2) Full sweep (US/EU/APAC) — 3/29 afternoon + 3/30 morning — collect TTFT/latency, concurrency curves
3) Controlled failover test — 3/30 afternoon — validate routing fallback and cache-warm behavior

I attached a compact MAP workbook with the measurement matrix and recommended runbook. Marissa will own instrumentation and the evaluation checklist; Karthik will run the stress harness and share raw CSVs.

Can you confirm that 3/29–3/30 works and share the external IPs or test hosts you want us to call from? If you prefer, we can run entirely from Redwood test agents (we'll share traceroute/ingress IPs).

Next step: once we have the sweep results we’ll add a short section to the MAP that maps findings to risk mitigations and a recommended close timeline.

Thanks —

Thanks — scheduling confirmed. Quick notes on instrumentation and checklist:

- Measurement matrix: TTFT (token-1), median/95/99 latency, tokens/sec, and error rate per model variant. We added a column for "streaming delta" (token-50 minus token-1).
- Concurrency harness: ramp to target concurrency over 10 min, hold for 15 min, collect heatmap. We’ll run each concurrency tier twice (cold and warm cache).
- Failover: simulate region outage by blackholing egress from Redwood agent in region; measure detection + reroute time and effect on in-flight sessions (expected behavior: new sessions routed to fallback replica, in-flight sessions try reconnect+resume).
- Artifacts: raw CSVs (per-region), per-run Grafana snapshots, aggregated readout PDF.

I've attached the final run command snippets and a compact checklist in the workbook. Karthik — please aim to publish the first-run CSVs by EOD 3/29 (PST). Tom — we'll publish results to the Drive link and a short confluence readout for your procurement team.

All — quick readout from the runs this morning/afternoon. Summary attached (readout-summary-ttft-latency-20270330.pdf) and raw exports in runcsv-us-eu-apac-20270329.zip. High level:

- TTFT (64-token chat-short): US-east median 48 ms, 95th 82 ms, 99th 130 ms. EU median 72 ms, APAC median 180 ms (Tokyo).
- Streaming delta (token-50 minus token-1): ~12 ms median across US runs, 18 ms EU, 30 ms APAC.
- Throughput at 300 concurrent sessions (mixed payloads): US sustained 2,800 tokens/s, model-specific backpressure observed at sustained 800-concurrency in APAC test (spike in queueing).
- Failover test (blackhole US-west agent): region detection + new-session reroute ~10–14s; cache warm time for equivalent TTFT ~45–60s depending on prompt template. In-flight reconnect behavior: sessions using streaming resumed within 6–10s but with partial token duplication in 2% of runs (edge case we can mitigate with idempotency token).

Action items and recommended mitigations:
1) For interactive 64-token chat, recommend routing policy: prefer US-east for NA users, EU for EU users; for APAC customers enable warm pool in APAC region at committed capacity to avoid cold-cache TTFT hit.
2) Add lightweight idempotency token to streaming frames to eliminate duplicate-token risk during failover.
3) If Acme expects >500 sustained concurrent sessions from APAC, recommend a quantized model variant for APAC shard or reserved capacity to avoid queueing spikes.

Tom — attaching the readout PDF and raw CSVs. If this looks good, Ben — we can map these findings to the MAP risks matrix and propose a close timeline: conditional green = 3/31 (Procurement review) -> contract execution by 4/07 assuming procurement sign-off.

Karthik
